interactions.hypothesis: BTTS-no is dominated by 0-0, 1-0 and 0-1 cells so rho changes the price more than lambda for low-scoring pairs.
Hot-keeper form regresses; the shrunk keeper effect, not recent clean sheets, should enter clean-sheet markets.
Missing first-choice defenders matter more for the team that already concedes openly; effect is convex in lambda.

The weaker side's P(score>=1) is 1-exp(-chances x conversion against this keeper): a high count of big chances only turns into BTTS-Yes if the opposing keeper's shrunk shot-stopping does not cancel it, so the keeper term scales the weaker side's chance-quality channel (direction: strong keeper cuts it).

Keeper effect applies only if the shrunk-rating starter actually plays; a backup keeper replaces a +0.05 PSxG-GA/shot starter with a replacement-level one, so the keeper term must be conditioned on the confirmed lineup, not season data.

Before the first goal the pairing behaves as in a static Dixon-Coles game; after it, the trailing manager's choice switches the match into an open regime, so the effective dependence is positive below one goal and may flip later in the match (hypothesis, timing not established from data).
Zero inflation is amplified when the focal striker is out: the same excess-FTS teams blank far more often without their one forward, while diffuse attacks barely move.

A weaker side with elite set-piece xG crosses a threshold at which its P(score) stays above the rating-implied level (the 0.55-0.6 figure is an unsourced hypothesis to be estimated) even against a dominant opponent; below the threshold it collapses to counter-attack luck.

For 2H BTTS the half-time state selects the second-half multipliers: a level half-time score keeps both rates near baseline, a one-goal lead raises the trailer's and lowers the leader's 2H rate, which raises P(trailer scores) but lowers P(leader scores), so the net effect on 2H BTTS depends on the asymmetry.

Only in cross-division cup ties: the lower-tier side's goal rate comes from the bridge rating gap, and a heavily rotated favourite (7+ changes) raises that rate and lowers its own clean-sheet probability, so BTTS Yes moves up most when a large tier gap coincides with heavy rotation; within-league fixtures are unaffected.

btts_and_clean_sheet.label: Both teams to score and clean sheet

First-half variant is lower-count and more dependent on the half split.
btts_and_clean_sheet.target: Both teams score at least once (full match or first half).

interactions.hypothesis: Direct meetings create negative dependence; common schedule creates positive dependence.
Frequent point ties make the tiebreak rule decisive.
Injuries hurt thin squads more; differential effect determines the pair.

P(leader holds) follows a normal tail in gap divided by sqrt(remaining fixtures times variance per match times (1 - rho)); correlation lowers the denominator, so the same gap gives a higher hold probability when the teams' results are positively correlated.

A remaining direct meeting is worth six points of swing; when the gap is at most three points it makes the meeting a decider, when the gap exceeds six it becomes irrelevant, so the effect of the meeting is conditional on the gap.

A shared European schedule hurts a thin squad far more than a deep one, so the relative strength shift is proportional to overlap times (1 - depth quality), generating gap changes of of unestimated size in the congested window (a hypothesis, not a measured effect).

Only on paths with equal final points does goal difference or head-to-head matter, so the tie rule has weight near the zero-point gap and none far from it; the effect is piecewise and depends on the league's order.

Uncertainty in each team's strength persists over all remaining fixtures (it is not averaged away), so the strength part of the gap sd grows linearly in games remaining while only the match-noise part grows with sqrt (variance quadratic vs linear), especially when one team has a harder schedule.

If both players' teams are likely to exit early, the two tallies concentrate on 0-1 goals and equality is likely; if one team goes deep its player's tally spreads out and equality falls, so the bracket paths drive P(equal) more than the scoring rates.

For KXWCTEAMH2H the two teams' stage outcomes are independent only if their bracket paths cannot cross before the final; when they share a group or bracket half, one's progress removes the other's, shifting mass away from 'same stage' at late rounds.

Finish-ahead contracts depend on two clubs' rest-of-season points; a club underperforming its rating has a raised dismissal hazard, and a dismissal switches its rating regime for the remaining fixtures, so the pairwise order probability is a mixture over change/no-change paths, mattering most when the two clubs are close and many matches remain.

interactions.hypothesis: Posterior strength uncertainty flattens favourites' title probability; fixed-strength sims overstate it.
Deep cup runs reduce league strength more for thin squads, making title and trophy futures negatively linked.
In tight races, head-to-head fixtures and tie-break order determine more of the outcome than average schedule difficulty.

For promoted or rebuilt clubs the preseason prior fixes the posterior mean while its width sets the tails: early in the season title odds of a mid-ranked contender are convex in prior width, and the prior weight fades as matches accumulate, so the interaction is large in the first third of a season and near zero afterwards (hypothesis on timing).

Whether the table converts to a champion by points or by playoff regime switches the sensitivity of title odds to regular-season strength; in playoff leagues rank 1 vs rank 4 differ by only a few percentage points while in pure leagues they differ by tens.

Cup and European progress costs league points in proportion to how thin the squad is: deep clubs rotate with little loss, thin ones lose several points of league expectation per extra competition round, so load times (1 - depth) predicts league slippage.
Cup outright odds are conditional on the draw: after the draw is made the same ratings produce different outright prices, and the effect is largest for strong teams drawn into the same quarter.

Exact group orders and any-nation-wins-group events depend on the joint table, where tiebreak order (head-to-head vs goal difference, fair-play points) decides discrete reorderings; a model with correct marginals but wrong tiebreaks mis-prices permutations far more than single-team group-win odds.

competition_winner_and_top_n.label: Competition winner, top-N and trophies

Multi-competition futures need a joint fixture-list simulation where one team's cup run affects its league strength. Top-N rungs must be consistent with winner and relegation probabilities, and rule wording (playoffs, ties) is decisive.
competition_winner_and_top_n.target: Winner or finish within the top N of a league/cup, or number of trophies, at the competition's end.

interactions.hypothesis: High-press teams get a larger first-half share, so period lambdas depend on style, not on a league-average split.
First-half draw probability is the intersection of dependence and low lambdas, so the two must be jointly modelled.
Second-half goal multipliers depend on half-time score and on bench strength after substitutions.

The second-half rate depends on the half-time margin and on who was favoured: a favourite trailing at the break lifts output strongly, while an underdog leading drops it, so the effect has opposite signs by role.

High-press teams front-load their chances; pairing a high-press side with a deep-block opponent (proxied by the opponent's PPDA and territory, since line height itself is not in free data) raises first-half expected goals more than the sum of the parts.

An early first-half goal produces the half-time margin that then selects the second-half multiplier: the opening-period hazard determines which state regime the 2H starts in, so P(2H total over 1.5) differs by who scored first and when (direction: a favourite conceding first lifts 2H output, an underdog scoring first lowers it).

A long first-half delay (VAR checks, injuries) adds exposure minutes: the extra time scales the half's expected goals proportionally (roughly one minute per 1/45 of the half rate; the size of a typical delay is to be measured) and matters most for close 0.5 total strikes.

Late lineup news (a missing first-choice striker) affects the opening-period rate more than the match average, because replacements need time and bench players are used later; the effect is conditional on the half.

Above a heat-index or altitude threshold the second half loses intensity (fewer high-intensity runs, more drinks-break pauses), so the first-half share of goals rises and 1H totals/1H BTTS gain probability relative to the full-match lambda; in temperate sea-level matches the split is unchanged.

first_half_and_period.label: First-half and second-half markets
first_half_and_period.mechanism: Half-window markets are the same goal process restricted to 45 minutes plus stoppage. The key parameters are each team's first-half goal share, early-match caution and the distribution of low counts (many 0-0, 1-0). Draws are very likely in first-half result markets, so dependence and draw propensity dominate. Second-half markets need conditional modelling from half-time state and substitution dynamics.
first_half_and_period.target: Result/total/handicap/exact score within the first or second half.

In second legs the aggregate decides which side attacks from kickoff; stage s3 and the interaction with soc.knockout_cagey_factor use it to shift the first-goal hazard and the no-goal mass.

The no-goal leg is the joint 0-0 cell of the goal-count model, so carrying it ties FTTS to the same model as the sibling match-result, totals and BTTS prices (stage s2).

interactions.hypothesis: Consistency between hazard integral and the 0-0 cell is a check on the goal model.
Dead-ball and penalty events provide step increments in hazard not captured by open-play xG.

The first-goal minute and route are jointly distributed: set pieces concentrate after minute 30 while penalties are timed by referee decisions, so the intensity decomposition changes the win-the-race probability and the minute distribution together.

Home advantage multiplies the intensity ratio, so in a neutral-venue final it disappears and the favourite's first-scorer odds fall by an amount to be estimated from neutral-venue finals relative to the same pairing at home.

Only in competitions that play extra time: the no-goal leg needs 0-0 at 90 and no extra-time goal, so its price is the product of the 0-0 cell and the tired-play survival over 30 minutes; in leagues and straight-to-penalties cups the extra-time factor is exactly one.

A referee with a high penalty-award rate raises the penalty share of first goals for the side that wins more box entries, so the route mix and the referee propensity multiply; the effect is largest when open-play xG is close and a single penalty decides the race.

In a second leg the aggregate decides who must attack: a side leading by two sits deep and the trailing side presses from kickoff, so the first-goal hazard is shifted toward the trailing team and the no-goal mass rises when the leader is strong enough to defend; the cagey factor is a function of the aggregate state, not a constant.

first_to_score_event.label: First team to score
first_to_score_event.mechanism: First-to-score is a race between two inhomogeneous Poisson processes with a null outcome for 0-0. The team with higher early hazard (press intensity, set-piece threat, penalty probability) is favoured beyond share of lambda, and the null outcome mass depends on low-score dependence. Rules for own goals and abandoned matches determine settlement.
first_to_score_event.target: Which team records the first goal over the entire game including any extra time (or no goal); First Team to Score series only.

interactions.hypothesis: Integrating lambda uncertainty fattens tails; ignoring it under-prices big margins and high scores.
Fitted rho and lambdas must be consistent with AH and total lines; residual score cells are the exact-score signal.
Late game chasing makes heavy favourites' margin distribution depend on bench depth and substitutions.

Rotation scales the favourite's attack, and the cross-tier gap sets the baseline; their product determines whether a cup mismatch is a 5+ goal margin or a tight win, so the combined effect is much larger than either factor alone.

Beyond a three-goal lead the match switches from a scoring regime into a damping regime for the leader, while a red-card collapse switches the opposite; the margin tail therefore has two regimes depending on which happens first.

Exact-score cells are determined jointly by marginal counts and the dependence correction; shifting rho changes 1-0/0-0/1-1 cells but leaves 3-1 unchanged, so the ladder must be fitted as a joint distribution, not rung by rung.

In lopsided leagues, rating uncertainty adds disproportionately to the probability of big margins because the convex tail of the margin distribution amplifies variation in the strength gap. (hypothesis: convexity of the margin tail in rating uncertainty is asserted, not measured)

Home advantage in the margin depends on the home side being at full strength; a rotated home favourite loses much of its crowd-driven edge over an organised underdog, so the venue term is conditional on lineup quality. (hypothesis, size unmeasured)

handicap_and_exact_score.label: Handicap and exact score
handicap_and_exact_score.mechanism: Handicap and exact-score markets are functionals of the full joint goal distribution: handicap prices need the goal-difference distribution including margins, and exact score prices need every cell. They are sensitive to the distribution tail, dependence parameters and lambda errors. Push/split rules for integer and quarter lines matter. The edge, if any, is more likely in consistency across rungs than in a lineup effect.

interactions.hypothesis: Lineup shortfalls reduce the attack/defence components separately, so a missing striker mainly lowers own goals and a missing centre-back mainly raises opponent goals.
Dead-rubber matches raise rotation, which changes both expected strength and the draw share.
Evenly matched teams at a strong-HFA venue convert draw mass to home wins; in neutral venues the draw share is higher.
Price comparison needs favourite-longshot and draw-bias correction to avoid false edges on the draw rung.

The result impact of a missing player scales with team dependence on him and with opponent strength; a surprise absence of a star in a close match moves P(win) by an unmeasured amount (a few points is a hypothesis) while the same absence in a mismatch barely matters.

Altitude adds to the home advantage once the visitor altitude gap exceeds about 500 m (the single breakpoint used throughout this record), rises roughly linearly above it and saturates for well-acclimatised sides near 3,000 m; the 500 m and 3,000 m values are hypotheses to be fitted, not established thresholds.
Rotation is most likely precisely when stakes are low and the next match is bigger, so rotation times (1 - leverage) predicts strength cuts; stakes alone does not.

Draw probability is determined jointly by the expected goal difference (peaks at 0), the total goals (lower totals raise draws) and rho; a rating-only model gets the ordering right but misprices the draw because it ignores total-goal environment.
In friendlies the effective rating gap is compressed (rotation, substitutions) and the variance is higher, so P(favourite win) is a flattened function of the rating gap.

League-estimated draw propensity applies only under the 11-a-side 90-minute regime; in all-star and small-sided formats the higher goal rate collapses the draw mass, so the draw input must be replaced, not adjusted, when the format profile changes.

interactions.hypothesis: Production is rate x minutes; minutes uncertainty dominates for fragile players.
Current leaders with large positive finishing delta should be shrunk toward xG-implied tallies.
A penalty taker's expected remaining goals include penalty xG, which can swing close races.

Expected goals is the factorisation team volume x share x minutes survival; the interaction of interest is that zero-inflated minutes make the exceedance probability of a rung lower than a mean-based Poisson suggests only when the mean is at or above the rung, and higher when the mean is well below it (the skewed minutes distribution widens both tails).

The probability of finishing first depends on tie rules: if ties split payouts, a candidate level with the leader has half the value, and if ties resolve on assists the playmaker striker gains; the gap-to-leader effect is conditional on the tie rule.

The expected future scoring rate is a shrunk mix of a hot finishing record and xG; the weight on realised goals decays with sample size, so equal over-performance is worth much less in a long remaining season.

Penalty duty adds roughly the team penalty rate times conversion (for example 0.15 team penalties per match x about 0.78 = about 0.1 goals per match) for the designated taker only; the gain is a product of the taker flag and the team penalty rate, not a threshold, and varies with referee and VAR habits.

Tournament tallies are per-match intensity times a random match count, and the two are positively correlated because a team advances partly through its striker's goals; ignoring this correlation under-prices high totals (record, 11+ goals) and over-prices middling ones.

interactions.hypothesis: Late-season matches where one side has nothing to play for reduce that side's strength, shifting the cut-off teams' probabilities beyond static ratings.
Advancement = 90-minute win + draw x (ET win + shootout); the required-goals state changes each term differently.
A deduction can move a team across the cut and alter tiebreak order, non-additively.

For qualification-settled series (KXUCLQUAL requires a main-tournament place per its text): a club finishing just outside the domestic Champions League places has a qualification probability that is a step function of whether a cup winner or coefficient slot frees an extra place, moving the cut line by one rank; rank-only series (last place, relegation) are unaffected.

Second-leg goal and draw rates depend on the first-leg lead: a two-goal leader plays deep, lowering both teams' rates, while a one-goal trailing team pushes; the advancement probability conditional on first-leg margin is nonlinear.

Last-place probability is convex in rating uncertainty because the minimum of several tightly clustered totals is more sensitive to variance than the mean; widening the posterior increases odds for the second-worst team more than it reduces the worst team's.
Direct clashes among survival rivals create paths where points tie; the tiebreak order then decides, so schedule effects interact with tiebreak only in narrow finishing scenarios.

A pending deduction or a final-day simultaneous kickoff changes the competitive regime: the deducted team goes from fighting for survival to a dead-rubber, shifting rotation and draw rates for its rivals. (speculative: for a deducted team still fighting relegation the effect may be the opposite; treated as a hypothesis to be tested only on observed deductions)

When two nations of the same set share a group, at most one can win it and their knockout paths diverge, which lowers the expected count reaching the knockouts and raises the chance that the set's furthest stage is decided by one team; independence over-prices 'all hosts qualify' or 'exactly N debutants' outcomes when set members are drawn together.

Relegation-zone clubs on a winless run have the highest dismissal hazard; a dismissal switches their rating regime for the remaining fixtures, so P(relegated) is a mixture over change paths and survival odds of a struggling club are not simply its current rating projected forward.

Promotion probability is piecewise in final rank: near-certain in automatic places, then a drop to the bracket win probability for 3rd-4th (semi only), and a further drop for 5th-8th if the 2026-27 six-team EFL format has an extra early round that 3rd and 4th skip (structure unverified, details pending); in Segunda, if a level tie after extra time goes to the better-placed side (secondary sources, unverified beyond that), rank matters more than under a shootout tie-break.

interactions.hypothesis: A draw-prone team has a different variance for the same expected points.
Rating uncertainty matters more with many fixtures left, and schedule matters more with few.
Margin markets must incorporate pending deductions affecting one team only.

A pending deduction on the leader or the runner-up shifts the first-minus-second gap by the deduction size, so a margin near 15 can cross the strike in either direction without any match being played; the effect is zero for clubs outside the top two.

The margin depends on whether the leader and runner-up still have to meet: a remaining direct meeting is a six-point swing that raises margin variance, while once both meetings are played the two totals evolve more independently through different schedules.

Points thresholds far above a club's expected total are convex in rating uncertainty: wider posterior strength fattens the upper tail, so 75+ for a club expected at 65 rises sharply with uncertainty while near-median thresholds barely move.

For three group wins the third game switches regime: a team already qualified after two wins may rotate, lowering its win probability, while a team needing a win plays full strength; this conditional dependence lowers P(3 wins) below the naive product.

A key injury during a congested stretch lowers expected points over many fixtures at once; below a squad-depth threshold the loss compounds with rotation, shifting the season total and, for contenders, the margin.

A club below its expected points has a raised dismissal hazard; a dismissal switches the rating regime for all remaining matches, so the season-points distribution is a mixture that is wider and left-skewed for struggling clubs, and a contender's change moves both its points threshold and the first-minus-second margin.

interactions.hypothesis: Tempo scales both teams' lambdas multiplicatively, so high-tempo matchups of two attacking sides produce more extra goals than additive terms predict.

A weaker keeper plus a rotated defence raises opponent scoring convexly.

A shared latent openness factor multiplies both lambdas, so Var(total) exceeds the sum of lambdas by a term growing with (lambda_H + lambda_A) squared: mismatches with a high summed lambda amplify the tail more than balanced low-lambda games.

A missing centre-back raises the total only if the opponent has strong attack ratings, and a missing striker lowers it only if the side's chances are concentrated in him; the lineup split effect is conditional on opponent attack quality from the ratings.
Tails switch regime with lead size: up to a three-goal gap totals grow, beyond it damping or collapse dominates, so tail multipliers must condition on the expected gap.

Heavy rain or wind lowers the effectiveness of high-tempo passing teams more than direct teams, so the weather effect on totals is scaled by the style of the teams playing. (speculative style interaction with no supporting evidence cited; hypothesis only)
Totals depend on both teams' finishing and both keepers; hot finishing against a hot keeper nets out; the joint distribution of finishing and keeper residuals sets the variance, not each separately.

The ladder of rungs must form a consistent distribution; kinks across rungs indicate pricing noise. Weather, referee and game state add smaller adjustments.

Qualitative stakes (title, survival, cup priority) that the leverage index quantifies.
Days of rest and travel feed fatigue and rotation expectations for both sides.
Tactical matchup residual visible once the XI is out.
Derbies compress goal margins and raise cards, nudging results toward draws.
Long trips matter in continental cups and tournaments, mostly for the away side.
Depth at the touch decides whether any model edge is executable.
Fee drag sets the minimum net edge for a trade.
Realised settlement labels for calibration of the model.

interactions.hypothesis: A rating built on full-strength XIs should be reduced in proportion to the confirmed XI shortfall; the interaction is multiplicative in the attack/defence components, not additive.
Low-leverage matches raise rotation probability, so the expected-XI shift is larger exactly when stakes are low and the effect on the draw probability is largest.
Strong home edge moves mass from draw to home win in evenly matched sides; weak-HFA venues (neutral, empty stadium) raise draw share.
The edge from comparing a model with sharp odds depends on correcting favourite-longshot and draw-price distortions, otherwise the apparent gap is a de-vig artefact.
Quote adaptation after lineup release measures how stale pre-XI quotes were and when informed flow arrives.

game_side.mechanism: Match-side markets (1X2, two-way, handicap, exact score, first-half and second-half results) are settled by the joint goal difference in a defined window. The mechanism is a latent attack/defence strength per team, adjusted for opponent and venue, converted to a goal distribution with low-score dependence, then modified by who plays (confirmed XI), rest/rotation, motivation and a game-state process. The market's sharp price carries much of this information, so the incremental inputs are those that arrive late or are mispriced (lineups, rotation, stakes) plus market-structure details.
game_side.target: Win/draw/loss or goal-difference threshold in regulation (or a half), as defined in the rules text.

inputs.why: Adjusted xG attack and defence give the two lambdas whose sum is the total.
The count distribution (over-dispersion and dependence) converts lambdas into ladder rung probabilities.
Low-score cells matter most for 0.5/1.5 rungs and BTTS.
Team-pair tempo and pressing change shot volume and openness.
Scoring-probability and clean-sheet propensities set BTTS and team-total rungs.
Keeper quality changes the conversion of shots on target to goals.
Starting lineup changes attack and defence strengths separately.
Wind/rain/heat mildly reduce quality and tempo.
Penalties add high-xG events with referee/VAR variation.
Set-piece xG is a persistent goal source for underdogs and in cagey games.
League-season goal baseline anchors the intercept of all lambdas.
Market-implied lambdas enable cross-rung consistency checks.
Cross-rung consistency exposes mispriced thresholds.
Historical realised frequency per rung checks calibration.
Open-play and set-piece xG for/against by team is the raw material of the lambdas.
Shot volume by game state gives tempo/volume cross-check to xG.
Corner volume reflects wing play and territorial pressure, correlated with totals.
Card/foul tempo and red-card risk change game flow and variance.
Attacking vs defensive formations change openness.
Confirmed lineups give the actual attack/defence units.
Rest and congestion alter intensity and rotation.
State-adjusted xG removes the bias of being ahead/behind in sampled matches.
VAR reviews shift disallowed goals/penalties and stoppage time.
Longer added time raises late-goal chances.
Liquidity by rung indicates which rungs are efficiently priced.
Realised totals for calibration by rung.

interactions.hypothesis: Two high-tempo teams raise total xG more than the sum of main effects, so tempo scales both teams' lambdas rather than adding a constant.
Wind/rain hurt possession-based high-press sides more than direct teams, so the weather effect on totals depends on style.
Over-dispersion and rho shape the whole ladder; a mis-specified distribution creates systematic residuals that look like per-rung mispricing.
Keeper changes interact with outfield rotation: a weaker defence in front of a weaker keeper raises opponent goal expectation convexly.

game_total.mechanism: Total-goal style markets (over/under rungs, team totals, BTTS, first-half totals) are determined by the sum of two correlated count processes. The mechanism is each team's expected goals (attack vs opponent defence), a dependence structure that handles low scores, a tempo/openness factor from both teams' styles, weather, referee/penalty tendencies and lineup quality, and game-state feedback (leading teams sit deep). Strength uncertainty fattens tails so high rungs are more probable than a plain Poisson implies.
game_total.target: Total goals (or team total / both-score events) in the contract's time window relative to a strike.

inputs.why: Decision calendars and base rates of leaks converting to announcements.
Transfer/manager news flow and club finances shape probabilities.
Administrative/regulatory processes follow official timelines.
Rules and eligibility criteria set which outcomes are possible.
Wording defines what counts as official confirmation and the cut-off time.
Price path reveals when leaks reached the market.
Order-flow around news windows shows informed trading.
Volume shows whether the price reflects much information.
Open/close/halt timing relative to the announcement date.
Manager statements timestamp announcements and intentions.

interactions.hypothesis: The probability that matters is the chance of an official confirmation inside the contract window, so base rates must be conditioned on deadline and wording.
Price jumps accompanied by signed trade imbalance indicate informed leaks; jumps without flow indicate stale quote repricing.

off_field.mechanism: Off-field and novelty soccer markets (transfers, managerial changes, rule changes, competition hosts, special events) are decided by committees, clubs and individuals rather than by on-pitch performance. The mechanism is information flow and incentives: reporters' leaks, deadlines, evaluation reports, club finances and political preferences. There is no standard predictive model; the useful inputs are timeline structure, base rates of rumour-to-confirmation conversion, resolution wording, and market microstructure.
off_field.target: A discrete announcement or event (appointment, host selection, transfer) that is formally confirmed by an official source before a deadline.

inputs.why: Half-specific share of goals converts match lambda into period lambda.
Team strength still drives the period difference, with larger noise.
Half-time distributions are low-count so dependence is large.
Second-half dynamics depend on first-half state and substitutions.
Timing of the first goal determines early-half outcomes.
Starters matter more in the first half before substitutions.
High-press sides front-load chances.
First-half draws are very frequent so draw modelling dominates.
Half definition (including stoppage time) and abandonment handling.
Period ladders must be consistent with full-time markets.
Team xG per half style gives the strength baseline.
Starting XI is what plays most of the first half.
Early corners reflect territorial pressure.
Early shot volume reflects tempo.

interactions.hypothesis: Pressing teams concentrate chances earlier, raising their first-half share; the period share depends on style not just league average.
Second-half goal rate is conditional on half-time score; the unconditional split averages over states that change risk-taking.
A high first-half draw share comes from both dependence and low lambda; they must be modelled jointly to price half-time draws.

period.mechanism: Period markets (first-half result/total/handicap/exact score, second-half result) are settled on a sub-window of the match. The mechanism is the same goal process cut by time: first-half goal rate is below the full-match average share, early dynamics are cautious, and half-specific dependence leads to many 0-0 and 1-1 first halves. Lineup information and game-state dynamics matter differently by half, and added time at half-time interacts with rules text.
period.target: Result/goal count within the first or second half under the wording of the contract.

inputs.why: Joint dependence between the two entities' outcomes.
Joint Monte Carlo gives P(A ahead of B).
Shared and independent strength uncertainty control tail probability.
Differences in remaining fixtures matter.
Differential injuries/suspensions shift relative strength.
Depth affects long-horizon relative strength.
Tie-break rule decides which entity is 'ahead' when equal.
Defines the metric, tie and void handling.
Sharp prices for each entity give a cross-check.
Team xG gives a performance-based cross-check on league position.

interactions.hypothesis: Direct meetings plus common rivals create dependence; P(A>B) differs from the ratio of marginal probabilities.
Ties on points occur frequently enough that the tiebreak rule changes the comparison probability materially.

player_other.mechanism: Head-to-head and other player/team comparison markets resolve on the relative performance of two entities (finish higher, score more) rather than absolute levels. The mechanism is joint simulation: two entities share the same league structure (direct match, shared rating uncertainty) so outcomes are dependent, and the relevant input set is differences in rating, schedule, injuries and the correlation structure rather than marginal probabilities.
player_other.target: Which of two teams/players ends ahead on a defined metric at a defined time.

inputs.why: Voting criteria, narrative and team success drive the choice.
Production totals feed the production component.
Underlying shot/chance production vs finishing luck.
Counting-stat race state matters for stat-heavy awards.
Team trophy probabilities flow into award probabilities.
Availability and minutes over the eligible window.
Injury risk for candidates before the vote date.
Eligibility window, voting body and tie rules are in the contract.
Bookmaker award prices aggregate narrative information.
Team strength context for award narratives.

interactions.hypothesis: Award odds are conditionally linked to team trophies, so probabilities must be computed jointly with competition outcomes.
Voters see goals not xG; counting stats inflated by finishing luck still win votes, so the regression term applies to the stats not the vote.

season_award.mechanism: Season-award markets resolve by voters or juries who combine production statistics, team success and narrative. The mechanism is a ranking function: individual production (goals, assists, xG, defensive actions), team trophies, tournament results, and exposure. Probabilities depend heavily on the awarding body's criteria and timing, and on the competing candidates' paths to trophies.
season_award.target: Winner of a named individual award decided by a defined panel/process.

inputs.why: Fixture-by-fixture Monte Carlo is the structural engine that maps strengths to season outcomes.
Strength posterior and drift determine tail probabilities and avoid over-sharp futures.
Order, venues and rival fixtures shift expected points among equal-rated teams.
Tiebreak order and slot allocation decide close cut-offs.
Sanctions shift points irrespective of on-pitch strength.
Depth affects strength under injuries and congestion over the horizon.
Current long-term absences adjust remaining-season strength.
Window moves and manager changes update stale ratings.
Early-season futures lean on priors until matches accumulate.
Multi-competition load links separate futures for the same team.
Leverage tells which remaining fixtures matter for the cut-off.
Sharp futures and match prices are strong priors for ratings.
Contract wording defines the exact qualifying outcome (including playoff/ET handling).
Top-N rungs must be consistent with winner and relegation probabilities.
xG-based ratings are less noisy than points for long-horizon strength.
Elo/Dixon-Coles ratings are the strength input to the simulation.
Late-season incentives change effort and rotation in simulated fixtures.
Postponed/abandoned fixtures reshuffle the schedule and can void markets.
Knockout advancement beyond 90 minutes includes shootouts.
Advancement-wording markets include extra time and penalties.
Aggregate state in two-legged ties.

interactions.hypothesis: Propagating strength uncertainty into the simulation flattens title/relegation probabilities relative to fixed-strength sims; the flattening is largest for the favourites and near the cut.
Schedule matters most when the table is tight and tiebreaks (H2H, GD) decide; the interaction is non-linear near cut-off.
Teams in multiple competitions with thin squads lose more strength in the league run-in, so depth interacts with cup progression.
A deduction changes who reaches a tiebreak and which tiebreak applies, creating non-additive effects in relegation and qualification markets.

season_outcome.mechanism: Season-outcome futures (title, top-N, relegation, qualification, advancement, outright, host, trophies) are the outcome of a stochastic tournament: remaining fixtures are simulated from team strengths with uncertainty and drift, then tiebreak and slot rules are applied. The mechanism is the aggregate of many match outcomes, so value comes from correct rating uncertainty, schedule strength, rule details, squad depth and injuries, and correlation across teams. Long-horizon prices embed more information drift than match prices, so the underlying rating prior and rule parsing matter most.
season_outcome.target: Final league position/qualification/advancement or trophy outcome, as defined by competition rules and the contract wording.

inputs.why: Full distribution (variance, skew) of points for threshold and margin markets.
Remaining opponents and venues set expected additional points.
Posterior strength uncertainty widens the distribution of totals.
Current tally, minutes and remaining fixtures set player race outcomes.
Player shot volume and shot quality produce expected remaining goals/assists.
Expected minutes are the largest uncertainty for player counting stats.
Penalty duty adds high-xG chances for scoring totals.
Observed over-performance should be shrunk toward xG-implied production.
Injury hazard truncates player and team output.
Draw variance drives dispersion of points totals.
Defines what is counted (league only, own goals, tie-break rules).
Threshold ladder must be consistent with distribution.
Team-level xG is the strength basis for expected points.
Dead-rubber effects on late-season points.
Shot volume supports player-level rate estimation.
Set-piece role contributes to scoring totals.

interactions.hypothesis: Expected goals scale with minutes times per-90 rate, so uncertainty in minutes dominates when per-90 rates are stable; the product is the primary mean driver.
A leader with large positive finishing delta is overrated by the tally; the gap to chasers should be reduced by the regression term.
Teams with higher draw propensity have narrower points variance for the same mean, so thresholds near the mean differ.

season_stat.mechanism: Season-stat markets (team points, points margin, player total, season leader) settle on an accumulated count over remaining fixtures. The mechanism is a sum of match-level processes (points or goals) with strength uncertainty, rotation and injury risk, and tie-break or rounding rules. Player stats additionally depend on minutes, role, penalty duty and finishing luck regression; team points depend on schedule strength and draw variance.
season_stat.target: A season-end count (points, goals, assists, margin) relative to a threshold or relative to another entity.

m.external_lines.label: Sportsbook/exchange reference prices
m.external_lines.measurement: De-vig each external quote (Shin for 3-way/long-shot-heavy sets, power for two-way), timestamp-match to the Kalshi quote, compute the Kalshi minus sharp probability difference and its sign persistence.
m.external_lines.mechanism: Sharp external prices are an information-rich prior; a Kalshi price that disagrees with the de-vigged sharp close either carries a stale quote or genuine information.
m.external_lines.rationale: The sharp closing line is the best-known single predictor in most sports markets, so any model must clear it, and its de-vigging method matters (proportional vs Shin vs power) especially for 3-way markets and long-shots. m.ladder_structure.label: Cross-rung consistency of the threshold ladder
m.ladder_structure.measurement: Collect all rungs of an event at one timestamp; check monotonicity of cumulative prices; fit a constrained distribution (bivariate Poisson / negative binomial for goals) by least squares on mid prices and record per-rung residuals and implied pmf.
m.ladder_structure.mechanism: Adjacent threshold markets (over 1.5/2.5/3.5 goals, handicap steps) must form a monotone cumulative distribution; violations or kinks expose mispriced rungs and the implied distribution of the underlying count.
m.ladder_structure.rationale: Each rung is priced separately by different participants, so the implied pmf (differences between adjacent cumulative prices) can go negative or be implausibly lumpy. Fitting a smooth parametric distribution across rungs and trading the residual is a market-structure edge that does not depend on a view about the teams. Subtle: push rules and integer vs half-point lines change which rung differences are legitimate.

soc.altitude_acclimatization_gap.label: Altitude difference between home venue and visitor's habitual altitude
soc.altitude_acclimatization_gap.measurement: gap_m = alt(venue) - A_vis, where A_vis = sum_k w_k*alt(venue_k)/sum_k w_k over the visitor's matches in the 60 days before kickoff (w_k=0.5^(days_ago/20)); if no match in window use altitude of the visitor's home venue. x = max(0, gap_m-500)/1000 (km above 500 m). Fit goal-difference ~ ... + beta*x (plus separate beta for 2H if minute data exist) on all matches since 2000 with team home-advantage and rating terms, ridge-shrink beta to 0 with k=50 matches above 500 m. As-of kickoff-1h; altitude values are static venue constants.
soc.altitude_acclimatization_gap.mechanism: Home altitude minus the visitor's mean altitude over recent matches, with recency of exposure.
soc.altitude_acclimatization_gap.rationale: Bolivia, Ecuador, Colombia and Mexico City host matches above 2,000-3,600 m; visiting teams from sea level lose 0.3-0.6 goals of expected margin, the effect is nonlinear in altitude and decays with acclimatisation days, and is outside the usual home-advantage parameter.

soc.xg.label: Team xG for/against, shot quality, set-piece xG
soc.xg.measurement: Per team-match: open-play xG for/against excluding penalties and own goals, set-piece xG separately; exponentially time-weight (half-life ~ 8-12 league matches, tuned by CV), adjust for opponent and venue via a ridge/hierarchical regression (see soc.xg_adjusted_ratings), shrink to league mean by n/(n+k) with k ~ 8-10 matches.
soc.xg.mechanism: Shot-quality-weighted chance creation and prevention is a lower-noise estimate of underlying goal-scoring ability than realised goals, which carry large finishing and keeper variance.
soc.xg.rationale: Goals are rare and noisy; xG counts what a typical finisher would score from the same shot locations, so the sum over a sample converges to future goal rate faster than goals do. Subtle: xG models differ by provider, xG should be split open play / set piece / penalty, and raw averages are biased by schedule and game state. Using it unadjusted for opponent and venue rewards teams that padded stats against weak opposition.

soc.xg_adjusted_ratings.label: Opponent- and venue-adjusted xG attack/defence ratings
soc.xg_adjusted_ratings.measurement: For each match, log(xG_for) ~ attack_i + defence_j + home + league intercept with ridge penalty (or Bayesian hierarchical with team random effects) fitted by rolling windows with exponential decay; evaluate by out-of-sample log-loss vs raw xG ratings.
soc.xg_adjusted_ratings.mechanism: A joint regression of per-match xG on team attack, opposition defence and home effects strips schedule effects so each team's rating reflects its quality, not its fixtures.
soc.xg_adjusted_ratings.rationale: Raw xG averages mix quality with opposition strength and with game state. A ridge/hierarchical model identifies attack and defence parameters with shrinkage that handles sparse samples and rotates through league structure. Subtle: cross-league comparisons need linking data, and using season-end ratings in a backtest leaks future results.

knockout_method_of_victory.label: Knockout tie method of victory/finish
knockout_method_of_victory.mechanism: A knockout tie decided in one match (a final, a single-leg cup tie, or the deciding match after an aggregate) is resolved in one of three ordered phases. Regulation (90 minutes plus stoppage) ends the tie when the score is unequal; otherwise 30 minutes of extra time are played, and a level score after 120 minutes goes to a penalty shootout. Method of Finish asks which phase ends the tie; Method of Victory asks which phase a named team wins in. The probability mass is generated by the regulation-draw probability (driven by the strength gap, the low total goal rate typical of finals and late risk aversion), the extra-time scoring rate under fatigue and extra substitutions, and a near-coin-flip shootout.
knockout_method_of_victory.target: Whether a knockout tie (or a named team's win) is decided in regulation, extra time, or a penalty shootout; covers finals with rules text plus 37 unlisted cup, super-cup, continental and league Method series.

The joint probability is the probability the player's team scores first times the player's share of that first goal (driven by minutes on the pitch, shot share and penalty duty), times the probability that a team leading first goes on to advance, which is high in knockouts but not certain because extra time and shootouts remain.

An injury to a rival in the candidate's own position frees a quota slot and raises his probability sharply, while an injury elsewhere does nothing; the effect is largest for the first reserve in that position.

Coaches keep their best XI until qualification is secured; once the stakes fall below a threshold (clinched group, third-place match) several changes happen at once, so squad players' start probabilities jump.
Call-up history predicts inclusion only under the coach who made those call-ups; a coaching change before the tournament resets the regime and pushes fringe probabilities toward a wider prior.

Injuries to listed players between the list and the first match create replacement slots; the probability that a given reserve is called depends jointly on the injury hazard of listed players in his position and on him being first in line.
A tier-one leak a day before brings most of the information; the official lineup then adds little except for rare late changes, so the value of further reports falls quickly.

For established core players call-up history alone decides inclusion; for fringe candidates and veterans with few recent camps, club minutes and match sharpness add information, so the club-minutes signal matters only in the middle of the call-up-history range.

player_squad_selection_and_lineup.label: Soccer squad selection and starting lineup
player_squad_selection_and_lineup.mechanism: Both contracts settle on a coach's list, not on play. A final World Cup squad is a fixed-size list drawn from a candidate pool by a coach who relies heavily on players he has repeatedly called up, subject to de facto positional quotas, the player's fitness at the deadline and, for veterans, the player's own decision to take part; late injury replacements before the first match add a path for reserves. A starting XI is the coach's match-specific choice given the opponent, fitness, suspensions and the stakes of the match, and is settled by who is on the field at kickoff.
player_squad_selection_and_lineup.target: A named player is included in a national team's officially announced final tournament squad, or in the starting XI at kickoff of a match.

inputs.why: Per-match win probabilities in order are the core input to a run-length calculation.

Residual serial correlation only, after drift from rating uncertainty, manager changes, summer reset and injuries is modelled; calibrate against out-of-sample streak frequencies so the clustering uplift is not counted twice.
Opponent-adjusted strength sets each match's win probability.
Uncertainty in team strength is shared across all matches and fattens the tails of the streak outcome.
Draws break a win streak; a draw-prone team has fewer streaks for the same points rate.
Venue ordering in the sequence changes which windows are winnable.
A manager change shifts strength and often produces a short-term run, a regime switch for the streak.
Key-player absences lower win probability over a block of consecutive fixtures.
Cup survival adds fixtures (often winnable early rounds) and congestion.
Which competitions count and whether a shootout win counts as a win.
Rules define the calendar window and all-competitions scope.
As-of run length and absorbing YES state.
Ordered fixtures across two seasons.
Summer change in strength for the autumn half.
Minutes load across league, cup and European fixtures lowers win probability and raises rotation inside dense blocks (Dec-Jan, cup runs).
Classifies cup ties drawn after 90 minutes (extra-time win versus shootout) under each scope reading of what counts as a win.

interactions.hypothesis: Positive serial dependence raises the streak probability most for mid-table teams whose per-match win probability is near 0.5, where independent runs of five are rare.
Clusters of home matches against weaker opponents create windows where a run is plausible; the same fixtures spread out yield fewer runs.
A manager change or summer rebuild resets the strength regime for all later matches at once, so the streak probability depends on a shared latent shift.

Positive autocorrelation lets good spells string wins together; the uplift over independent trials is largest when per-match win probability is moderate (0.45-0.6) and small for dominant teams that streak anyway.

A block of home fixtures against weaker opponents produces a high-probability window; the same fixtures interleaved with away matches at strong sides produce fewer complete windows, so order changes the result at constant average difficulty.
A manager change or summer rebuild moves strength for all later matches at once; if the shift is positive, autumn windows become far more likely to contain a run, otherwise the spring half dominates.

A team already on a three- or four-win run with winnable next fixtures is close to settlement, while a team with no run needs a fresh five-match window; the probability jumps when the run length crosses three.
In cup ties a draw after 90 minutes leads to extra time and possibly penalties; under a reading where only 90/120-minute wins count, draw-prone teams lose streaks in cups even when they advance.

team_win_streak.label: Team consecutive-win streak
team_win_streak.mechanism: The contract settles YES if somewhere in the calendar year the team wins at least N matches in a row across all competitions. The outcome is generated by an ordered sequence of match win probabilities (each well below one, with draws as frequent streak-breakers), the number of matches available before the year ends, and serial dependence from form, injuries and manager changes that makes good and bad runs cluster. The probability of a run of length N is a highly convex function of the typical per-match win probability, so modest changes in team strength or schedule order move it a lot; once the run is achieved the contract is settled.
team_win_streak.target: Whether a team strings together at least N consecutive wins across all competitions within a stated period.

inputs.why: Per-team scored/conceded rates against the drawn opponents and the simulated knockout path settle the named-team ladders, Goals Allowed and the most/fewest extremes.
Group plus 32-team bracket simulation supplies matches played per team, champion identity and knockout pairings used by most series.
International attack/defence strength is the base of every match rate and of champion and pairing probabilities.
Goals per match level times 104 matches sets the Total Goals strike (308+ needs about 2.96 per match).
Shared tournament effects widen the totals distribution beyond independent matches.
Match-level goal count distribution is the building block for sums and maxima of match totals.
Tail of single-match totals drives the knockout Highest Scoring Game strike.
Mismatch mix of fixtures moves group goal totals, blanks, hat tricks and high-scoring games.
Per-round shootout counts (exactly N / N+ in R32, R16, QF) and group winners lost in the R32 come from round-level bracket simulation.
Per-tie probability of level after 120 minutes feeds every shootout-count series.
Knockout goal-rate and draw-rate multiplier changes shootout counts and the KO highest-score maximum.
Round count of each shootout settles Longest Penalty Shootout and when goalkeepers kick.
Team shootout skill slightly shifts shootout length and goalkeeper-kicker exposure.
Opening-goal timing per match sets the Fastest Goal minimum and early concession hazards.
Kickoff ET timestamps plus per-minute concession hazards settle the four-team Concede First race.
P(champion never trails) needs champion identity times conditional trailing along its path.
Recovery after conceding feeds the champion-never-trails calculation.
Excess blank rates of the weakest attacks dominate Every Team to Score.
Joint W/D/L patterns inside a group settle Group Points (all four teams on 4 points).
Draw frequency in balanced group fixtures is required for the all-on-4-points pattern.
Player-level goal distributions settle Hat Trick count, Club Goals maximum and Goal in Every Game.
Per-match base rates for direct free-kick, olimpico and goalkeeper goals settle the rare-event series.
Player npxG/90 and shot share drive hat-trick and every-round scorer probabilities.
Expected minutes of key forwards cap team and player goal ladders.
Star-forward absence moves named-team goal ladders and player-pool aggregates.
Designated free-kick and corner takers drive direct free-kick and olimpico rates.
Qualification state before matchday 3 drives rotation and attacking intent in named-team ladders.
Dead-rubber versus must-score leverage moves weak teams' blank probabilities in round three.
Longer added time raises goals per match for Total Goals and team ladders.
Penalty award rate adds goals and feeds goal-environment estimates.
VAR penalties and disallowed goals shift the per-match goal level.
Heat and Mexico City/Guadalajara altitude act on a subset of venues and raise or lower rates.
Per-series flags: group vs full tournament, ET in or out, shootouts out, own-goal attribution, third-place game in.
Exact wording per series fixes strike construction (N+, exactly N, $1/N dead heats) and scope.

interactions.hypothesis: A full-tournament team ladder is a random sum: goals per match times a random number of matches, so advancement depth and attack strength compound and the upper rungs are convex in strength.
A shared tournament effect shifts every match together, so Total Goals has fatter tails than an independent sum of 104 matches.
The longest shootout is a maximum over a random number of shootouts, so per-round shootout counts and sudden-death continuation must be simulated jointly.
Never-trailing is evaluated on the eventual champion only, so it mixes over champion identity and conditioning on winning lowers trailing rates.

The chance of a very high-scoring match rises convexly with the strength gap, so a knockout bracket that keeps a few heavy mismatches in the R32 lifts the KO Highest Scoring Game rungs more than the same average gap spread evenly.
A tournament-level random effect makes Total Goals a mixture, so the 104-match sum has fatter upper and lower tails than independent matches; rungs far from the mean such as 308+ are most affected.

The longest shootout exists only if at least one tie reaches penalties and long ones need sudden death; with about four or five shootouts per tournament the maximum and the chance a goalkeeper kicks are driven jointly by count and length.

A full-tournament team ladder equals goals per match times matches played; stronger teams score more per match and play more matches, so high rungs (e.g. 22+ for France) respond multiplicatively to strength while group-stage ladders do not.

Champions that trail must come back, so conditioning on the title selects paths with few or recovered deficits; the never-trailed probability is far above the product of unconditional per-match trailing rates for a favourite.

In the Concede First race, a team whose first match ends before another team kicks off wins outright if it concedes at all, so the race is a threshold on kickoff order: earlier calendar position dominates defensive strength unless the early team keeps a clean sheet.

A weak team still without a goal entering matchday 3 with qualification hope chases harder; one already eliminated may not, so the Every Team to Score conjunction is sensitive to round-three incentives of the few binding teams.

tournament_aggregate_event_props.label: Tournament aggregate and match-event count props
tournament_aggregate_event_props.mechanism: Twenty-two settled 2026 World Cup series, each a different statistic of the same 104 matches (72 group, 32 knockout incl. third place): a tournament goal sum; named-team goal ladders over the group stage or the full run (3 to 8 matches); extremes across teams or groups with $1/N dead heats; per-round shootout counts and the longest shootout in rounds; the highest-scoring knockout match and the fastest goal; group-table patterns and group winners lost in the Round of 32; a cross-match race to concede first by ET timestamp; whether the champion ever trails; and player or rare-event aggregates (hat tricks, club goal pools, a player scoring in every knockout round, direct free-kick, olimpico and goalkeeper goals). Outcomes come from team strengths against the actual draw and simulated bracket, the international goal environment, shootout kick dynamics, player shares of team goals, and contract scope flags.
tournament_aggregate_event_props.target: A count, sum or extreme of goals or match events aggregated across many matches in a tournament, relative to a strike or condition.

inputs.why: Joint probability the two named teams occupy the same match (any round, a named round or the final) is the settled quantity for four of five series.
Maps group positions and best-third combinations to knockout slots and rounds, the structure every World Cup pairing uses.
Joint cross-group finishing distribution including the best-third ranking feeds slot occupancy.
Group and knockout simulation produces the joint paths from which pair meetings are counted.
International and club strength ratings set each match probability that fills the bracket.
Group tie-breaks and best-third criteria decide slots near the cut.
Single-leg World Cup ties and two-leg Champions League ties, incl. ET and shootouts, decide who advances.
Champions League league-phase rank distribution determines which clubs enter the knockout bracket and where.
UEFA rank-to-bracket-line mapping fixes which side of the Champions League bracket each finisher is on, so whether two clubs can only meet in the final.
Aggregate state between legs updates Champions League advancement during the knockout rounds.
Opponent strength along a team's World Cup path sets its reach probability per round.
Remaining group permutations during the group stage move slot probabilities.
Long-term absences of key players adjust team strength for advancement.
Risk that scheduled host-city games are moved or cancelled settles the location series.
Abandonment or postponement of the specific scheduled games in a host region can leave a location unplayed.
Exact wording fixes any-match vs named-round vs final, settlement at qualification, the No Team outcome and the location granularity.

interactions.hypothesis: Whether two teams from different groups can meet in a given round depends on the best-third combination that qualifies, so pair-meeting probability needs the joint cross-group distribution pushed through the slot graph.
Two Champions League clubs on the same bracket side can only meet before the final, so P(final pairing) is near zero for same-side finishes and multiplicative across rounds for opposite sides.
A host location settles No only if every scheduled game there is moved or not played, so the location probability is a near-certain base state with a small joint failure regime.

Whether two teams from different groups can meet in the R32 or R16 depends on which other groups supply qualifying third-placed teams, so pair-meeting probabilities from independent group marginals pushed through the graph misstate cross-group pairings.

Teams level on points flip group position at a hard tie-break threshold (head-to-head before overall goal difference per secondary reports), moving a team onto a different bracket side and changing which pairings are possible.

A late-round meeting requires both teams to win every feeding tie, so per-round advancement probabilities multiply along two paths; modest per-round edges compound into large differences in Semifinal pairing odds.

In the Champions League, two clubs whose league-phase ranks put them on the same bracket side can meet before the final but never in it, so the final-pairing probability is zero for those rank combinations and positive only for opposite sides.

With several scheduled games per region, individual abandonments almost never empty a region; NO needs a region-level relocation regime, so the location probability is a mixture of a near-certain base state and a rare switch driven by dated news.

tournament_bracket_composition.label: Tournament matchup composition and host venue
tournament_bracket_composition.mechanism: Pair-matchup contracts settle the moment both named teams qualify for the same match: in any World Cup match (group co-membership is fixed by the draw, otherwise the pair must converge in a knockout slot), in a named World Cup round (Semifinal, USA Quarterfinal with a 'No Team' outcome), or in the Champions League final after the league phase, two-leg knockout rounds and a fixed bracket. Probabilities come from the joint group, best-third and knockout simulation pushed through the official slot graph. The location series is different: it settles on whether a scheduled game is actually played in Mexico or Massachusetts before 20 July 2026, a host-venue relocation and cancellation risk unrelated to results.
tournament_bracket_composition.target: Whether a named pair of teams is confirmed as the matchup in any match, a named round or a final (settled at qualification), or whether any tournament game is played in a named host country/state.
